chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who takes a pledged item for one hundred dirhams while it is worth three hundred dirhams, then destroys it. Is the man required to return two hundred dirhams to its owner?
He عليه السلام said: "Yes, because he took a pledge in which there was surplus value and then caused its loss."
I said: If half of the pledged item is destroyed? He عليه السلام said: "According to that proportion."
I said: Then should they return the surplus value between them? He عليه السلام said: "Yes."

key_terms.الرَّهْنَ: the pledged property held as collateral
key_terms.بِمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ: for a debt amount of one hundred dirhams
key_terms.ثَلَاثَمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ: the full market value of the collateral, three hundred dirhams
key_terms.ضَيَّعَهُ: caused it to be lost or destroyed through neglect or liability
key_terms.عَلَى حِسَابِ ذَلِكَ: to be calculated in proportion to the amount destroyed
key_terms.فَضْلٌ: the surplus value of the collateral beyond the secured debt

ai.seo_question: If collateral is worth more than the debt and it is destroyed, must the excess value be repaid?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on pledged property whose value exceeds the debt it secures. If the pledge is destroyed, the holder is liable for the excess value beyond the debt, and if only part is destroyed, liability is calculated proportionally.
